messages:
support-queue: Customer AcmeHealth is hitting intermittent 502s on hosted inference since ~2024-06-04 18:00 UTC. They report TLS handshake timeouts and gateway 502s. Example trace: cid-9f8e1a2. Raising for triage.

maya: Can we get the raw customer error sample + trace logs and the endpoint they called?

support-queue: Pasted from customer (redacted):
```
error: 502 Bad Gateway
cause: tls_handshake_timeout
trace_id: cid-9f8e1a2
client_ip: 18.203.4.77
edge: eu-west-1-edge-22
request: POST /v1/generate
```
Customer says issue started after they rolled a new internal proxy (corporate appliance) but also we had a cert rotation yesterday evening.

jordan: Quick hypothesis: corporate proxy might be rewriting/stripping SNI or interfering with TLS session resumption, leading to our edge failing handshake and returning 502. Any NXDOMAIN or resolver flaps during that window?

sree: From edge logs I pulled resolver responses around the trace time: we saw short-lived NXDOMAIN for hostnames like model-s-23.acme.svc.redwood.internal during cert rollover. Example dig run from edge host: 
```
$ dig +short model-s-23.acme.svc.redwood.internal @1.1.1.1
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
Also seeing TCP RSTs to port 443 from the corporate ASN in the packet logs.

alice: Ask customer to run these two quick repro commands from behind their proxy and attach output: 
```
# DNS check
dig +short @8.8.8.8 model-s-23.acme.svc.redwood.internal\n
# TLS check
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-hosted.com:443 -servername api.redwood-hosted.com -brief
```

ben: I'm enabling verbose tls.debug = true on the eu-west-1-edge-22 pool for that customer and will add a temporary fallback route to the dedicated pool (no shared SNI routing) to see if it fixes. :wrench:

support-queue: Customer ran openssl, attached paste: "SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood-hosted.com:443". Their proxy logs show repeated entries: 
```
[proxy] action=strip_sni target=api.redwood-hosted.com src=10.10.1.23
```
They confirmed the new appliance has an "SNI normalization" feature enabled by default.

jordan: If proxy strips SNI, our edge cannot select correct cert/route causing handshake aborts. Two parallel tracks: 1) Ask customer to disable SNI rewriting (recommended) or add a bypass for redwood hosts. 2) Short-term: pin the customer to IP-based routing/dedicated endpoint that does not rely on SNI.

sree: Also, the cert rotation we did yesterday briefly created a mismatch for endpoints that were served by fallback routing; combined with intermittent NXDOMAIN it likely triggered the observed spike. We'll correlate cert push timeline with resolver metrics.

netops-bot: Alert: egress-resolver-errors (eu-west-1) spike at 2024-06-04T18:12:14Z, 5m avg error rate = 12% (baseline 0.7%).

maya: Action items: 1) Support to ask customer to disable SNI rewrite and run the dig/openssl commands. 2) Ben to verify fallback routing applied and monitor for resolved 502s. 3) Sree to correlate resolver NXDOMAIN window with our cert rotation and post exact windows. 4) If the customer cannot change proxy immediately, propose dedicated endpoint migration. I'll schedule a short call with AcmeHealth for 2024-06-05 16:00 UTC. I can own the follow-up postmortem if we confirm the cert/resolver/proxy interaction. :white_check_mark:

ben: Temp route applied to dedicated pool at 2024-06-04T19:03:12Z for AcmeHealth. Monitoring.

support-queue: Customer confirmed disabling SNI normalization on their appliance fixed the immediate 502s in our slack thread. They will run longer load test overnight and report back.

maya: Thanks team. If customer reports any regressions please ping this thread and attach tcpdump + openssl output. For tcpdump ask them to run: 
```
sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/acme-443.pcap host api.redwood-hosted.com and port 443
```
Then gzip and share.

jordan: Will add a short doc snippet to docs/known-issues about "SNI rewriting appliances" and guidance to use IP pinning/dedicated endpoints as mitigation.

support-queue: Closing initial escalation, moving to follow-up after monitoring.
